## 1. Questions, prior exposure and frozen decisions

- State the depth and persistence hypotheses, criteria and alternatives. Cite the signed plan/data-plan dates,
  fingerprints and amendments. Record public-report and teaching exposure, and show how source records, your own
  derived measurements and fixed selection rules support an analysis that another person can reproduce.

## 2. Data and comparable reference regions

- Give the source versions/cutoff, event/station/window inventories, exclusions, usable observing time and gaps.
  Explain how reference regions were selected before outcomes and matched for measurement quality.

## 3. Depth measurements and uncertainty

- Show the direct-P/S baseline and phase selection, synthetic recovery, depth scans and uncertainty.
  Report sensitivity to geometry, velocity model, missing phases, nearest station and starting conditions.
  Separate formal errors from model/selection uncertainty and retain poorly resolved events in the accounting.

## 4. Template matching and independent validation

- Describe the frozen bank and tuning/validation partitions. Give held-out and injection recovery, missed cases,
  noise-only false alarms, duplicate merging and independent candidate checks. Measure the dependence on template
  families, stations, signal size and noise/gaps, including what the bank could not detect.

## 5. Persistence, bursts and completeness

- Show rates/occupancy per usable observing time, completeness by epoch and magnitude, and the result with and
  without bursts under the frozen rule. Propagate detection errors and gaps; compare reference regions under the
  same rules. Distinguish background, bursts, a mixture and unresolved evidence according to the criteria.

## 6. Decisions and what could change them

- For each hypothesis give the measured metric, uncertainty, threshold and decision, with the notebook or script
  that prints each number. Identify planned changes that reverse a result and ambiguities that remain.

## 7. Comparison with the Suncheon project

- Compare the measurements and detector limits of both projects. Which design or data-quality differences permit
  the comparison, and which limit it? Describe what is learned when the projects agree or differ without assigning
  an expected answer to either one.

## 8. Reproduction and next observations

- Name the archived inputs/fingerprints, commands, environment and run records needed for reproduction.
  Show an unchanged rerun and the planned sensitivity runs. State the observation that would resolve the most
  important remaining uncertainty and whether obtaining it is feasible.
